findings.claim: The five F23 JDBC Project rows are assigned only to future overlay metadata, while their sole learning vehicle is a later course lab that remains a candidate. The next day is already framed as JDBC review and assessment. This plan can therefore reach review before any guaranteed teach-and-do experience for connecting Java to PostgreSQL, prepared statements, transactions, repository replacement, and database-backed testing.

evidence.section: Lesson: JDBC Basics (connections, SQL statements, prepared statements, transactions)
Using the Driver: Connecting to the Database

findings.recommendation: Keep the frozen F23 rows as one project rather than creating new topic pages, but make the F23 course project lab a required intake commitment rather than a candidate. Give that project row observable objectives covering all five existing syllabus rows, bind those objectives to the course lab, and sequence the lab before the F24 JDBC review and module check.

findings.claim: The lab plan says every lab, including the project named "Connecting Java to Postgres with JDBC", uses embedded H2 and that graded tests never depend on PostgreSQL. H2 PostgreSQL compatibility mode emulates only a subset of PostgreSQL differences; using it as the only assessed environment does not let learners demonstrate the named real-tool outcome and makes the required PostgreSQL installation largely disconnected from practice.

evidence.section: Compatibility / PostgreSQL Compatibility Mode (a subset of differences is emulated)
Using the Driver: Connecting to PostgreSQL with JDBC URLs

findings.recommendation: Use a learner-local PostgreSQL database, created and dropped by the lab, for the F23 JDBC project and for PostgreSQL-specific objectives. H2 may remain only where the author and SME can show the exact targeted behavior transfers; do not claim it covers psql commands or PostgreSQL-only seeding/planner behavior. This remains container-free and follows the existing lab contract.

findings.claim: The check promises coverage of JDBC, but all coding is described as short SQL tasks. Its only JDBC mappings are review objectives o2 and o3 (SQL-injection explanation and transaction choice); it omits JDBC review o1 (connect, prepare, execute, read, close) and has no objective for the F23 repository replacement or database-backed testing. The most authentic F23 skills therefore cannot be demonstrated by the blueprint.

evidence.section: Lesson: JDBC Basics (establishing connections, processing SQL statements, prepared statements, transactions)
Using the Driver: Initializing the Driver and Connecting to the Database

findings.recommendation: After the F23 project row has objective-bearing lab metadata, revise the representative coverage so the coding format elicits at least one central JDBC/project outcome, not SQL alone. Preserve the frozen MCQ + coding formats, 45-minute block, and pass mark; keep platform resource policy deferred.

findings.claim: Objective o3 adds result pagination with LIMIT and OFFSET to the frozen "Filtering and sorting" topic, and the blueprint selects this added objective while selecting neither the filtering nor sorting objective. PostgreSQL documents LIMIT/OFFSET separately from sorting, so this both expands the syllabus and skews assessment away from the named topic.
findings.recommendation: Remove pagination as a required objective. Keep the page focused on WHERE and ORDER BY, for example by making o3 predict deterministic ordering with explicit sort keys, and map the blueprint to a filtering or sorting objective already named by the frozen syllabus.
